title: War Room: Incident Communication Templates & Checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of concise communication templates and the internal war-room checklist for incidents that impact Redwood Inference production services. Focus is on fast, accurate public/status updates, clear customer-facing language, and an internal checklist to keep the war-room coordinated.

Audience:
- On-call SRE/engineer leading the incident
- Incident commander (IC) and communications owner (comm-owner)
- Customer success / account leads for affected customers
- Partner/Legal/Security when escalation required

Goals for communications:
1) Be timely — initial acknowledgement within 10–15 minutes for Sev1/S2
2) Be clear — what is affected, who is investigating, and what customers can expect now
3) Be consistent — single source of truth (status page + slack incident channel)
4) Surface next steps and ETA when available
5) Minimize ambiguity and avoid speculation

How to use this doc (quick):
- IC picks a comm-owner. comm-owner posts to status.redwood.ai and the incident slack channel.
- Use the short templates below verbatim where possible. Add details in the body after the template.
- Update cadence: every 15m while active, then 30m -> hourly as things stabilize.

Triggers for using templates:
- Service degradation impacting >5% of customer queries or causing errors for a hosted API region
- Site-wide outages or persistent increased latency above SLOs for >5 minutes
- Data plane failures that may affect customer data integrity (immediately escalate to legal/compliance)

Quick incident metadata to gather (first 10 minutes):
- Incident ID: SRE-INC-YYYY-NN (create in Linear/Jira)
- Scope: services/regions affected, percentage of requests or number of customers impacted
- Start time (UTC): 
- Who is the IC: name + slack handle
- Primary on-call/engineer: name + slack handle
- Temporary mitigation (if any): e.g., failover enabled, traffic redirected
- Link to logs/dashboards: (add links)

Status Page Templates (copy/paste):
- Initial Acknowledgement (Sev1/Sev2) — short form
  Title: [Investigating] Degraded API responses in US-West (incident SRE-INC-2025-023)
  Message: We are investigating reports of increased errors and timeouts for the Redwood Inference hosted API in US-West. Some requests may fail or be delayed. Engineers are actively triaging. We will provide an update within 15 minutes.
  What we know: (brief bullet) e.g., 1) Errors began at 2025-03-02T14:07Z 2) Errors are HTTP 500 / timeouts 3) Impacting ~12% of requests
  Where to watch: https://status.redwood.ai

- Update (progress) — follow-up status to paste into status page body and the incident slack channel
  Title: [Update] Mitigation in progress — routing traffic to fallback fleet
  Message: Engineers have identified a regression in the autoscaler that caused overloaded worker pools. We have started routing traffic to a fallback fleet and error rates are trending down. Expected additional updates in 15 minutes.
  Next steps: Continue routing, validate KV cache consistency, observe error rate drop below SLO
  ETA: ~25 minutes (subject to change)

- Resolved (final)
  Title: [Resolved] API errors in US-West (incident SRE-INC-2025-023)
  Message: The issue causing elevated errors and timeouts for the hosted API in US-West has been resolved. Traffic returned to standard fleet and error rates are back within normal ranges. Incident start: 2025-03-02T14:07Z; resolved: 2025-03-02T14:53Z. A post-incident summary will be posted to Confluence with root cause and remediation actions.

Customer-facing Email Template (short, for affected customers)
- Subject: Incident update: degraded inference performance in US-West (SRE-INC-2025-023)
- Body: Hello — we are reaching out to let you know that some requests to Redwood hosted inference in US-West experienced elevated error rates and latency between 2025-03-02T14:07Z and 2025-03-02T14:53Z. Our engineers identified the cause (autoscaler regression) and applied a mitigation that returned services to normal. We do not believe any customer data was corrupted. We’ll share a post-incident report with details and any recommended actions. If you saw production errors, please reply with your request IDs and we’ll prioritize follow-up.
- Close guidance: route customers to their account lead if they need a technical deep-dive or SLA credits.

Internal Slack War-room Checklist (one-page cheat sheet)
- Step 0: Create incident channel #inc-SRE-YYYY-NN and link Linear/Jira issue
- Step 1: Fill initial incident metadata (see above) — IC or comm-owner
- Step 2: Post initial status page and one-liner to #inc channel using the ‘Initial Acknowledgement’ template
- Step 3: Assign roles explicitly (IC, comm-owner, mitigation lead, customer-ops lead, data lead)
- Step 4: Collect proof points and attach logs/dashboards (links)
- Step 5: Execute mitigation plan and post every 15m: current state, next action, ETA
- Step 6: If outage >=30m or customer-impacting tiers, escalate to Head of SRE and PSE (use escalation matrix below)
- Step 7: When resolved, post a final status on status.redwood.ai and in #inc channel; ensure customer emails are drafted
- Step 8: Kick off postmortem within 72h and assign owner for RCA

Escalation matrix (quick)
- On-call -> IC -> Head of SRE -> CTO (for incidents >4h or data integrity concerns)
- Customer-facing escalation: customer-ops lead -> account exec -> VP of Customer Success (for enterprise accounts)

Checklist items for comm-owner (details):
- Use simple language, avoid technical jargon in public messages
- Include incident ID and short scope line in every update
- Don’t promise ETA until confirmed by mitigation lead
- If unsure about data exposure, add explicit line: ‘We are investigating potential data impact and will update as soon as possible.’
- Coordinate with legal/security before acknowledging any data loss or breach

Examples of short one-liners for Slack thread (can copy/paste):
- [INC SRE-INC-2025-023] Investigating increased errors in US-West; engineers triaging; update in 15m
- [UPDATE] We identified overloaded worker pools; routing to fallback fleet; error-rate down 30%
- [RESOLVED] Service restored; more detail in postmortem next steps

Templates for longer post-incident customer summary (postmortem email)
- Title: Post-incident report: SRE-INC-2025-023 - US-West hosted API error spike
- Executive summary (2–3 sentences): What happened, who was affected, customer impact summary, and high-level root cause
- Timeline: bullet list of key timestamps and actions taken
- Root cause: short explanation + contributing factors
- Mitigation and resolution: what was done to restore service
- Customer impact: guidance on what customers might have seen and how to verify
- Remediation & prevention: planned and short-term fixes, owners, ETA
- Contact: account lead + support link

Open questions / TODOs in this draft:
- Confirm exact cadence for updates for Sev2 incidents (15m vs 30m?) — proposal: 30m after initial ack unless customer escalates
- Add template variants for Dedicated/Private deployments (region names and wording differ)
- Decide whether to auto-cc legal for any incident marked ‘data-impact’
- Add a small checklist for monitoring/customer telemetry owners to proactively notify top 10 enterprise customers after detection

Notes and references (internal):
- Slack incident channel naming conventions: #inc-SRE-YYYY-NN
- Reference runbooks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/incident-process
- Pager/rotation: see on-call roster (linked in Confluence)

Author notes (working):
- This is intentionally concise — push for short public updates and fuller postmortems.
- Keep templates minimal so comm-owner can publish quickly.
- We should run a tabletop exercise to validate cadence and the templates with CS legal and SRE in the next on-call rotation.

Revision history:
- 2025-03-02: initial draft (Priya Nair)
- 2025-03-06: added customer email template + internal checklist (Jordan Alvarez)
- 2025-03-10: updated escalation matrix and linked artifacts (Maya Gupta)

Unresolved: Need approval from Head of SRE and Legal before moving to ‘final’ status.
